Hi Daniel — thanks for the read-through and good questions. Below are concise answers you can paste into your inventory. I attached our completed SIG encryption PDF and a concise rotation matrix for reference.

Key custody model (hosted Redwood API):
- Redwood operates a multi-tenant hosted offering where envelope encryption is used. Customer data is encrypted with per-tenant Data Encryption Keys (DEKs). DEKs are themselves encrypted (envelope-wrapped) with a Key Encryption Key (KEK) that is HSM-protected.
- For the hosted service the KEK is managed by Redwood in FIPS-validated HSMs (we use Thales nShield / HSM cluster) — the KEK is never exported in plaintext.
- We support an opt-in BYOK/Customer-Managed KEK model for Enterprise customers: customers can provide a KEK via a supported KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) or an HSM-backed key that Redwood can reference via a secure key reference (no key material is transmitted). When BYOK is enabled, the customer holds the KEK and Redwood stores only envelope-wrapped DEKs.

Rotation cadence and customer impact:
- DEK rotation: DEKs are rotated automatically per-tenant on a 90-day default cadence; can be shortened to 30 days for high-risk workloads. Rotations are performed as background re-wraps with zero downtime (rolling rewrap using the current and next KEK, and replay protection).
- KEK rotation: KEKs are rotated on a 12-month cycle by default; emergency rotations are supported (e.g., key compromise). For Redwood-managed KEKs the rewrap operation is performed by the HSM cluster with an audit trail; rotation does not require customer interaction.
- BYOK customers control their KEK rotation policy; when the customer rotates a BYOK KEK they notify Redwood via the secure key reference update API and we perform a staged rewrap of DEKs. There is no application downtime — we use dual-keystore rollover windows to ensure requests succeed during transition.

Networking & in-transit controls (brief):
- All control and data-plane traffic uses TLS1.3 with strong cipher suites; public endpoints require mTLS for dedicated/private deployments.
- Inter-service links between front-ends and inference workers use mutual TLS and ephemeral session keys; we use strict cipher suite and TLS config baselines.

I pasted the short inventory-ready lines below that you can drop into your SIG: 
- "Data at rest: customer data is encrypted with tenant-scoped DEKs; DEKs are envelope-encrypted with KEKs stored in FIPS-validated HSMs (Redwood-managed) or customer-managed KMS/HSM when BYOK is enabled. KEKs are not exportable in plaintext."
- "Rotation: DEKs rotated by default every 90 days (configurable), KEKs rotated annually by default; rotations are implemented as online rewraps with no planned downtime. Customers using BYOK manage KEK rotations and notify Redwood for staged rewraps."

Let me know if you need the wording to be even shorter for a tick-box inventory.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Security & Compliance (Ops)
Redwood Inference

Adding a couple technical notes that might be useful to Acme's architects: 
- HSM details: our HSM cluster runs network-attached Thales nShield modules with FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated hardware security. Private keys used for KEKs are generated inside the HSM and marked non-exportable.
- Envelope scheme: DEKs are AES-256-GCM; KEKs wrap DEKs using RSA-OAEP or a KWP variant depending on HSM capability (we prefer AES-KW for internal flows when supported).
- Egress & proofs: we provide signed key attestation artifacts and HSM certificate chains (attached) and can run a joint review with your cryptography team if you require hardware attestation for BYOK onboarding.
- Replay protection & migration: during rotation we use per-record sequence metadata and a short-lived transitional key window so older tokens are rejected after a defined grace period (configurable).

If Acme wants a one-page cryptography memo for procurement, I can draft it — short, non-technical, and focused on custody and risk.

-rishi
Principal Applied Cryptographer
Redwood Inference
